newsitem.title: USA: Marsh & McLennan sees J&H deal accretive.
newsitem.headline: Marsh & McLennan sees J&H deal accretive.

text.p: Marsh & McLennan Cos Inc executives said they expect the acquisition of privately-held insurance broker Johnson & Higgins to be additive to earnings in the first full year of operation.

The deal, which is expected to close in the second quarter, is expected to contribute a couple of percentage points to earnings in the first year but then "move to double digits" in the third year, Marsh & McLennan chief financial officer Frank Borelli told analysts on a conference call.
Marsh & McLennan shares rose 4-1/2 to 126-1/2 in mid-morning trading.
Marsh & McLennan said it expects analysts' 1997 earnings estimates to change only slightly as a result of this acquisition.
Marsh & McLennan also said it to achieve annual pre-tax cost savings of at least $150 million.
The company told analysts it expects return on equity to continue to exceed 20 percent and said it expects positive cash flow in the first full year of operations.
The company also said it expects to achieve double-digit return on its investment in Johnson & Higgins in the second full year of operation.
The company also estimated goodwill at about $1.3 billion or 30-35 million on an annual basis.
Marsh & McLennan chief executive A.J.C. Smith said the company was pleased with its Putnam asset management business and plans to expand it.
"We think it's a splendid business," Smith said. He said he did not believe this deal starves Putnam of resources and said he expects to grow it through acquisition or other ways.
However, he said the future of Johnson & Higgins' Unison partnerships was still unclear.
Johnson & Higgins' global network includes exclusive relationships with Unison partners in more than 150 cities around the world.
"We really haven't been able to address that thoroughly yet," Smith told analysts.

"Clearly there are some fine firms in Unison that we would be happy to be associated with. In other places, Marsh & McLennan already has very substantial operations and it would perhaps not make sense for it to be larger," he said.
However, Smith said he believes Johnson & Higgins will complement Marsh & McLennan's current business.
Marsh & McLennan will gain a strong position in the Netherlands through the acquisition of Johnson & Higgins as well as strength in the U.S. retail middle market.
Johnson & Higgins also will bring strength in certain professional areas, such as health and construction, Smith said.
Marsh & McLennan also said it expects its share repurchase program will continue in place.
The company said its stated policy has been that any free cash flow generated from operations is kept available for purchasing shares.
When enough cash is accumulated, the company said, it will look at market conditions and consider the question of a new repurchase program.
